params.body:
## Why

`App\Http\Middleware\Access` only ran its rights check when the session happened to carry
the key `MT_ACCESS`. The whole block hung on `$request->session()->has('MT_ACCESS')`, so an
authenticated request that arrived without that key passed the middleware unchecked: the
route was allowed and the four shared variables simply read as `false`. The rights model
therefore degraded silently to "allow the route, draw no buttons" instead of denying. A
screen without buttons still answers with 200, and every POST/AJAX endpoint behind the same
middleware answered too.

## What MT_ACCESS is

The rights of the logged-in user, per menu security key, in the shape

```php
['export' => ['view' => 1, 'add' => 1, 'edit' => 1, 'delete' => 0], ...]
```

Only rows with `view == 1` are in it (a menu that is absent means "may not see it"), and
`home` and `import` are added for everyone. It is computed from `role_access` joined to
`menus` for the role of the user.

Who writes it: `LoginController@authenticated`, and nothing else. Who reads it: this
middleware, and `App\Http\Helpers\LinkHelper` for the menu.

What the middleware did with it, per case, before this change:

| case | today |
| --- | --- |
| route name without a dot | no check, variables `false` |
| MT_ACCESS present, menu has `view == 1` | variables from the rights; `create/store` needs `add`, `delete/destroy` needs `delete`, `update` needs `edit`, else redirect to `home.index` |
| MT_ACCESS present, menu absent or `view == 0` | redirect to `home.index` (a guest would redirect to `login`) |
| **MT_ACCESS absent** | **no check at all: the request is let through, variables `false`** |

## When it is absent

Any authenticated session that did not pass through `LoginController@authenticated`: a
session whose data was lost or partially flushed while the auth cookie stayed, a remember-me
cookie, a session created another way, any future code path that logs a user in without
calling that one method (`Auth::login`/`loginUsingId` elsewhere), or an API/Passport-
authenticated request that reaches a web route. `UserController@loginAs` is fine today: it
flushes, logs in and calls `authenticated()` itself. The point is not how likely each path
is, it is that a check may not hang on a key any of them can omit.

## What changes

- `App\Support\AccessRights` holds the computation that used to live inside
  `LoginController@authenticated`: `forUser($user)` builds the rights of a user from the
  database, `current()` returns the rights from the session and rebuilds+caches them when
  the session has none. One place, used by both callers, no copy.
- `LoginController@authenticated` now calls `AccessRights::forUser()` and writes the result
  under the same key. The computed value is identical, line for line; it was moved, not
  rewritten.
- `Access` no longer conditions its check on the session key. When the session has no
  rights it rebuilds them for the logged-in user and runs the normal check on them. With no
  logged-in user there is nothing to rebuild and the request is denied the way the
  middleware already denies a guest: `redirect()->route('login')`. No new response shape,
  no `abort()`, and no path that passes unchecked.
- The rebuilt rights are stored in the session under the same key, so this costs one query
  on the first request of such a session and nothing afterwards, and `LinkHelper` gets the
  menu it was also missing.

## Stale rights (second finding, not changed here)

Nothing refreshes `MT_ACCESS` after it is written. Changing a role's rights in
settings/access, or moving a user to another role, writes `role_access`/`users` and touches
no session: the user keeps the rights of their login until they log out and back in. That is
true before and after this change (this PR only adds one more moment where the rights are
read fresh: the first request of a session that has none). Fixing it is not a one-liner, so
it is not in this PR: it means either dropping the session cache and reading the rights per
request, or invalidating the sessions of every user of a role when its rights change. Worth
a decision of its own.

## What cannot change

No user loses anything they can do today. The rebuilt rights are exactly what a fresh login
writes for that user, from the same tables through the same repository; a session that
already carries rights is still judged on what it carries and reads nothing from the
database. The only behaviour that moves is the case that was the hole: a session without
rights on a route its role may not see is now denied instead of let through.

Four existing test classes seeded no rights and relied, without saying so, on the check
being skipped (`OwnVehicleAuthorizationTest`, `StocklistDetailPreviewTest`, `KlantmodusTest`,
`OwnStockListTest`). They build their users straight in the database, without `role_access`
rows, so they now put in the session what a real login would write for that menu. What they
test (the ownership check in the controller, the price leak, the render) is unchanged.

## Checked

- New `tests/Feature/AccessWithoutSessionRightsTest`: a session without `MT_ACCESS` on a
  route its role may not see is denied (verified that this test returns 200 and fails on
  `origin/main`); the same session on a route its role may see gets 200 with the delete
  button following the database right, and without the right the button stays away; the
  rebuilt rights land in the session; a session that carries rights is still judged on
  those, in both directions; `forUser(null)` is null.
- `tests/Feature/ExportListAccessTest` (from #268) keeps its point: the list still renders
  with rows and no rights in the session, now with the role's view right in the database.
- `php artisan view:cache` clean, `php artisan test` green except `BuildStampTest`, which
  fails the same way on `origin/main` in this local checkout (no build stamp present).
params.title: Access: no request passes the rights check because a session key is missing
